card.title: Animalia: Level of organization, body plan, body symmetry…

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Animals are compared by organisation, symmetry, body plan, germ layers, coelom and segmentation. Sponges are cellular and asymmetrical. Cnidaria are radial, diploblastic and blind-sac. Flatworms are bilateral and acoelomate. Roundworms add a pseudocoelom and a complete gut. Annelids add a true coelom, lined by mesoderm on both sides, and metameric segments.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Cellular, tissue, organ, organ system.
Acoelomate flatworms, pseudocoelomate roundworms, eucoelomate annelids onward.
Blind sac: one opening. Tube within a tube: mouth and anus.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: A blind sac and a tube-within-a-tube are different plans. Hydra and a liver fluke have one opening. Ascaris and an earthworm have a mouth and an anus.  ·  A pseudocoelom is not a true coelom. In Ascaris the cavity is not lined by mesoderm on the gut side.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Diploblastic stops at Cnidaria in this course. Every phylum from flatworms on is triploblastic.  ·  Sponges are left asymmetrical. Do not force a symmetry on Sycon.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Sycon is cellular and irregular in shape, with a canal system rather than a gut.  ·  Hydra is radial, diploblastic, and a blind sac.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: This note stops at the body characters. The classes inside each phylum are the next note.  ·  Germ-layer words here are ectoderm, endoderm and mesoderm only.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Build a four-column table for sponge, Hydra, liver fluke, Ascaris and earthworm.  ·  Write one sentence that defines a true coelom without using the word coelomate.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Flat none, round false, ringed true: acoelom, pseudocoelom, eucoelom.  ·  One hole is a blind sac. Two holes is a tube.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Q.** What is the difference between a pseudocoelom and a true coelom? **Answer.** Both are body cavities between the gut and the body wall, but they differ in **lining**: | Basis | Pseudocoelom | True coelom (eucoelom) | |---|---|---| | Position | Persistent **blastocoel** cavity | Cavity arising within mesoderm | | Lining | Gut side…  ·  **Q.** Why is cephalisation linked to bilateral symmetry and not to radial symmetry? **Answer.** Bilateral symmetry creates a **head end that meets the environment first** — moving in one direction, the animal encounters food, danger and mates frontally, so nervous tissue, sense organs and mouth concentrate there (cephalisation).…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: A five-mark answer is a table: animal, level, symmetry, coelom, segmentation. One row each is enough.  ·  Define the coelom before you use the word eucoelomate. The lining is the whole definition.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Levels of organisation  ·  Symmetry and cephalisation  ·  Blind sac and tube-within-a-tube  ·  Three grades of body cavity

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Cellular (Porifera), tissue (Cnidaria), organ (flatworms), organ system (roundworms onward).  ·  Asymmetry, radial symmetry, bilateral symmetry with cephalisation.  ·  Blind sac versus tube-within-a-tube.  ·  Acoelomate, pseudocoelomate, eucoelomate.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Echinoderm larvae are bilateral even though the adult is radial.  ·  The coelomic fluid of an earthworm is a hydrostatic skeleton: muscles squeeze it, and the segment changes shape.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **Q.** Name the level of organisation of a sponge, a Hydra, a liver fluke and an earthworm. **Answer.** | Animal | Level of organisation | |---|---| | Sponge (Porifera) | **Cellular** — no true tissues | | Hydra (Cnidaria) | **Tissue** — diploblastic, nerve net | | Liver fluke (Platyhelminthes) |…

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Pheretima is bilateral, triploblastic, eucoelomate and metameric, with a mouth and an anus.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: A true coelom is a cavity → B  ·  Hydra's gut is a blind sac because → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Animalia is sorted, before any phylum name is used, by a short list of body characters: how the cells are organised, the body plan, the symmetry, the number of germ layers, the body cavity, and whether the body is segmented. Two animals that look nothing alike can still sit near each other if those characters match.…  ·  Level of organisation runs cellular, tissue, organ, then organ system. Porifera stop at the cellular level: the cells divide labour, but they do not form true tissues. Cnidaria reach the tissue level. Platyhelminthes reach organs, such as a pharynx and flame cells, without packing those organs into systems the way a worm with a closed blood system does.…  ·  Symmetry is the way a body can be cut into matching halves. Most sponges are asymmetrical. Cnidaria are radial: several planes through the oral-aboral axis give similar halves, which suits a life of waiting for food to arrive from any side. From flatworms onward the body is bilateral. One plane only divides it into left and right, and the front end gathers sense organs.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Metamerism  ·  Metamerism is serial segmentation, clearest in the earthworm.  ·  Adult starfish look radial, but they are eucoelomate and their larvae are bilateral. Radial symmetry does not put them with Hydra.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Proglottides of a tapeworm are not metameric segments. Metamerism, as used here, starts in Annelida.  ·  Organ level and organ-system level are not the same grade. Flatworms have organs. A complete gut plus a body cavity is the organ-system grade.  ·  Radial symmetry in Cnidaria is a primary condition. Radial symmetry in an adult starfish is secondary.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A true coelom is lined with mesoderm on both the body wall and the gut.  ·  Bilateral animals have one plane of symmetry and a front end where sense organs collect.  ·  Level of organisation, symmetry, coelom and segmentation are decided before the phylum is named.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: For Hydra, Ascaris and Pheretima, state symmetry, germ layers, coelom and body plan. **Answer.** | Animal | Symmetry | Germ layers | Coelom | Body plan | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Hydra** | Radial | Diploblastic (ectoderm + endoderm) | None (acoelomate) | Blind sac — one opening | | **Ascaris** | Bilateral |…  ·  Say what 'lined on both sides by mesoderm' rules out. **Answer.** It rules out a **pseudocoelom**. In Aschelminthes the cavity is a persistent blastocoel: the gut side is **endoderm**, only the body-wall side is mesoderm.…  ·  Explain why a tapeworm's pieces are not counted as metamerism. **Answer.** The tapeworm's **proglottids are buds**, not true segments: each is a **reproductive unit budded off** from the neck, containing its own complete set of reproductive organs, with no repetition of the other organ systems and no common body…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Body plan names the layout of the gut. Sponges are a cell aggregate with canals, not a gut. Cnidaria and flatworms have a blind sac: one opening both takes food in and puts waste out. From roundworms onward the plan is a tube within a tube.…  ·  Germ layers and the coelom decide how much space the organs have. Diploblastic animals, the cnidarians, have ectoderm and endoderm with jelly between them. Triploblastic animals add mesoderm. Flatworms are acoelomate: mesoderm fills the space as a solid parenchyma, and there is no body cavity.…  ·  Segmentation, or metamerism, is the repetition of body units that each carry a share of the same organs. It is the annelid character, and it continues in arthropods and chordates.…
